answer_1.quote: A core component of our proposed STYLEDISTANCE approach is a LLM that generates a synthetic dataset with controlled content and style. The dataset is composed of pairs of sentences which are paraphrases of each other (i.e. their content is similar) but differ in style.
answer_1.outputs: pairs of sentences which are paraphrases of each other but differ in style

answer_2.quote: We also run automatic evaluations to assess other properties of the dataset: • Content Similarity measures the average semantic similarity between the positive and negative parallel examples ). • Fluency measures the average fluency of our examples using a classifier trained on CoLA . • Diversity uses the score proposed by  to measure how different each generated text is from every other in terms of content/topic using semantic similarity.

answer_4.quote: Each instance was annotated by 10 different annotators from a pool of 73 graduate students in a NLP class.
answer_4.guideline: We measured the extent to which humans judge our positive examples do contain the desired style feature and our negative examples do not.
criteria: presence of desired style feature in positive examples
absence of desired style feature in negative examples
